# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_018_page_001.jpg

---

**18:1** But your holy ones had a very great light, and those others heard their voice but did not see their form — and because they too had not suffered the same things, they counted them blessed.

**18:2** And because they, who had previously been treated unjustly, did not harm them, they gave thanks; and begged pardon for the fact that they had been at variance with them.

**18:3** Instead of this you gave them a blazing pillar of fire as a guide for their unknown journey, and a harmless sun for their glorious exile.

**18:4** For they deserved to be deprived of light and to be kept in darkness, those who had imprisoned your sons, through whom the imperishable light of the law was going to be given to the age.

**18:5** When they had planned to kill the infants of the holy ones, and one child had been exposed and saved, as a reproach to them you removed a multitude of their sons, and destroyed them together in a mighty torrent.

**18:6** That night was made known beforehand to our fathers, so that they, knowing with certainty what oaths they had trusted, might be of good courage.

**18:7** The expectation of your people was the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies.

**18:8** For by the same thing by which you punished our adversaries, you glorified us when you summoned us.

**18:9** For holy children of good men offered sacrifice in secret, and put into effect with one accord the divine law, that the holy ones would share alike both in the same good things and in the dangers; and they were already singing the praises of the fathers.

**18:10** But the discordant cry of the enemies rang back; and a pitiful lamentation for the children was spread abroad.

**18:11** And the slave was punished with the same penalty as the master, and the commoner suffered the same as the king.

**18:12** So all together, with one form of death, were the dead beyond counting. For the living were not even sufficient to bury them, since at a single stroke the most prized generation of these people was destroyed.

**18:13** For while they had disbelieved everything on account of the enchantments, at the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged that the people was son of God.

**18:14** For while gentle silence held all things, and the night was in the middle of its swift course,

**18:15** your all-powerful word leaped from heaven, from the royal throne, a stern warrior into the midst of the land of destruction,

**18:16** bearing a sharp sword, your irrevocable decree — and it filled all things with death; and while it reached to heaven, it stood upon the earth.

**18:17** Then at once apparitions in dreadful dreams greatly disturbed them, and unexpected fears came upon them.

**18:18** And one here and another there, thrown down half-dead, made clear the reason for their dying:

**18:19** for the dreams that had troubled them announced this beforehand, so that they might not perish without knowing why they suffered.

**18:20** But the experience of death also touched the righteous, and a plague struck the multitude in the desert; yet the wrath did not remain for long.

**18:21** For a blameless man hastened to their defense, and bringing forward the weapon of his particular ministry — prayer and the propitiatory incense — he withstood the wrath and put an end to the calamity, showing that he was your servant.

**18:22** And he subdued the wrath, not by bodily strength and not by force of arms, but by the word he subdued the chastiser, appealing to the oaths and covenants given to the fathers.

**18:23** For when the dead had already fallen on one another in heaps, he intervened and held back the wrath, and cut off the way to the living.

**18:24** For on his long robe the whole world was depicted; and the glories of the fathers were on the four rows of stones, and your majesty was on the crown upon his head.

**18:25** To these the destroyer gave way, and these he feared; for it was sufficient to test the wrath only by these.
